content: MYCOBUTIN Capsules contain rifabutin, an antimycobacterial agent classified as a semisynthetic ansamycin antibiotic derived from rifamycin S. Each capsule is formulated for oral administration and contains 150 mg of rifabutin, USP. The inactive ingredients in the formulation include microcrystalline cellulose, magnesium stearate, red iron oxide, silica gel, sodium lauryl sulfate, titanium dioxide, and edible white ink. The chemical name of rifabutin is 1',4-didehydro-1-deoxy-1,4-dihydro-5'-(2-methylpropyl)-1-oxorifamycin XIV, as per the Chemical Abstracts Service (9th Collective Index). Its stereochemical designation is (9S, 12E, 14S, 15R, 16S, 17R, 18R, 19R, 20S, 21S, 22E, 24Z)-6,16,18,20-tetrahydroxy-1'-isobutyl-14-methoxy-7,9,15,17,19,21,25-heptamethyl-spiro trienimino)-2H-furonaphth imidazole-2,4'-piperidine]-5,10,26-(3H,9H)-trione-16-acetate. Rifabutin has a molecular formula of C46H62N4O11 and a molecular weight of 847.02. It is a red-violet powder that is soluble in chloroform and methanol, sparingly soluble in ethanol, and only very slightly soluble in water, with a solubility of 0.19 mg/mL in water. The compound has a log P value of 3.2, which represents the base 10 logarithm of its partition coefficient between n-octanol and water.
